hook.text: In 2015 Oxford Dictionaries named 😂 the Word of the Year. A picture had become a word.

buildup.text: Shigetaka Kurita created the first emoji set in 1999 for Japanese mobile phones—176 tiny symbols.

discovery.text: Emoji function as tone markers in text. They don't replace words—they replace facial expressions and gestures.

twist.text: The same emoji means different things across cultures. A thumbs-up is positive in the US but offensive in Iran.

climax.text: Courts now admit emoji as evidence. A gun emoji followed by a person emoji has been used in threat cases.

punchline.text: Emoji is the first truly global visual pidgin.

quiz.question: Who created the first emoji set?

details.summary: Emoji have evolved from cute additions to text messages into a proto-language used by billions. They convey emotional nuance that text lacks, create cross-cultural communication shortcuts, and are constantly evolving through user innovation.
details.whyItMatters: Emoji demonstrate that humans will always find ways to add emotional and social nuance to communication. They represent the latest chapter in the eternal story of evolving human expression.
takeaways: Over 10 billion emoji are sent daily across platforms
The Unicode Consortium decides which emoji are officially created
Emoji meanings vary dramatically across cultures and generations

faq.question: Are emoji really a language?
faq.answer: Emoji lack grammar, syntax, and the ability to express abstract concepts independently — they are not a full language. But they function as a supplementary communication system that adds emotional context, tone, and nuance to text.

faq.question: Who decides which emoji exist?
faq.answer: The Unicode Consortium — a non-profit dominated by tech companies (Apple, Google, Microsoft) — decides which emoji get coded into systems. Proposals go through a formal review process.
